seed: Objects of type `reflection` under action ACTION1 with touching neighbours [reflection,target] show mixed outcomes: h,pixels,w x1, gone x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a field of the object itself, such as its tags, pixels, visibility or layer. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Single horizontal mirror axis (wall row block A) plus 3x3-block pieces and static targets; ACTION5 cycles axis -> pieces -> axis; ACTION1/2 move the selection x-/+3, ACTION3/4 move y-/+3 (the axis ignores 3/4).
Moves are blocked by board bounds and piece overlap; reflections map block b to 2A-b, skipped on piece blocks and off-board.
Render layers wall1<target2<reflection3<piece4 (holes show the solid below, else 0 if selected / 4 for reflections), then re-extract; wall/player names rank among components plus 0 pixels of other types.
The reflection 'gone' outcome under ACTION1 is a re-extraction merge: piece_0 touches piece_1, so the pieces and their reflections become single 4-connected components. No object field decides it.
Unconfirmed: what ACTION5 selects after the first piece (only axis->piece_0 observed). Also passes 30/30 with hidden state disabled.
